facts.text: The clone registers MultiagentSimple-v0 with entry point multiagent.envs:SimpleEnv and max_episode_steps=100
The clone registers MultiagentSimpleSpeakerListener-v0 with entry point multiagent.envs:SimpleSpeakerListenerEnv and max_episode_steps=100
make_env builds a MultiAgentEnv from a scenario's make_world, reset_world, reward and observation callbacks
The simple scenario has one movable agent that is silent and does not collide, and one landmark that does not move or collide
The world has two position dimensions, a 0.1 s timestep and damping 0.25
The physical action space of a movable agent is Discrete(world.dim_p * 2 + 1)
discrete_action_input defaults to False, whose comment describes the action as a one-hot N-dimensional vector
With discrete_action_input true, action 1 sets the x force to -1, 2 to +1, 3 sets the y force to -1 and 4 to +1
The physical action is multiplied by a sensitivity of 5.0 when agent.accel is None
A reset draws the agent and landmark positions uniformly from -1 to +1 and zeroes their velocities
The observation concatenates the agent velocity with each landmark position relative to the agent
The reward is the negative squared distance between the agent and the first landmark
The world integrates velocity with damping and force/mass*dt, then position with velocity*dt
An agent's mass is 1.0, its motor noise is None and the world applies noise only when u_noise is set
MultiAgentEnv.step returns per-agent observation, reward and done lists plus an info dict
MultiAgentEnv.reset calls the scenario reset callback and returns a list of per-agent observations
A missing done callback makes every done flag False
The observation space is a Box from -inf to +inf with shape (obs_dim,) for each agent
make_env without benchmark passes no done callback to MultiAgentEnv
The README says the code base is an archive and that the maintained version is PettingZoo

determinism.notes: reset(seed) and cap.world.seed.v1 fix the fake's initial state, after which its integration is deterministic; upstream draws the initial positions from numpy's global generator (simple.py:34-38) and has no env seed parameter, so one seed gives different trajectories on the fake and upstream

gaps: the fake serves the single-agent simple.py scenario only: one movable silent agent and one immovable landmark; communication, the speaker-listener registration and the other scenarios of the clone are not modelled
the clone has no multiagent/envs.py, so the two registered ids cannot be constructed at the pinned commit; the fake stands in for make_env('simple') and the sim backend path was not run

the upstream default discrete_action_input is False and its step expects a 5-element action vector, while its action_space is Discrete(5); the fake applies the discrete_action_input=True mapping of environment.py:164-167 so the declared integer action is meaningful

the fake draws positions with Python's random.Random and integrates Python floats; upstream draws from numpy's global generator and returns float32 arrays, so one seed does not reproduce an upstream trajectory

the fake returns the Gymnasium (observation, info) reset pair and a five-value step tuple; upstream returns a list of per-agent observations and a four-value step tuple, and the bridge normalizes both
the class's reset options object is accepted but has no effect: the simple scenario's reset_world takes no options

no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction, actuator, sensor or noise model: the fake integrates the simple momentum equations directly and the simple scenario disables collisions; the agent has no motor noise and the fake adds none
no rendering, viewers, render.modes or PassiveEnvChecker, and no wall-clock pacing (realtime_factor 0)
the fake was not compared with an upstream run: gym and numpy were not installed where the gate ran and the clone was never imported
snapshot and restore are not offered: the upstream class and the fake expose no get_state/set_state
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
